Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for yesterday's demo — the performance looked promising. Before we move forward we need a short evidence package and a few explicit written assurances for our privacy/compliance review:

1) A short summary of how Redwood handles customer-provided PHI in hosted deployments (data flows, encryption at rest/in transit, KMS handling).
2) An explicit statement we can include in our DPIA confirming Redwood will not use customer prompt/response content to train or improve models for other customers (we need the legal/technical phrasing).
3) Confirmation of retention windows for prompts and generated responses (default + options to shorten), and whether ephemeral prompt caching for latency is persisted to disk.
4) Copy of the latest SOC 2 Type II report (redacted) or a location where we can verify it.
5) If available, the CAIQ export and any HIPAA attestation language you provide to customers.

We'd like the package by EOD Friday 21 May if possible. We may also ask for a signed DPIA acknowledgement form.

Alex —

Appreciate the clear ask. We'll assemble a compact evidence bundle and an explicit no-train statement you can include in your DPIA. Quick notes up front:

- Redwood hosted customers can opt into customer-isolated routing; by default we do not use customer prompts to train open-model weights, and we can provide a signed acknowledgement for your records.
- Prompt/response retention defaults to 30 days for troubleshooting and abuse detection; we offer configurable retention down to 0 days for enterprise customers with Dedicated or Private deployments. Ephemeral caching used for latency (KV cache) is memory-first and not persisted to customer-visible long-term stores unless customers enable logging.
- We'll share the SOC 2 Type II summary and a CAIQ export; Rishi will drop the artifacts and a short technical write-up into this thread.

Targeting EOD 21 May. If you'd like the DPIA acknowledgement signed, please indicate the signatory name and we'll route to Legal.

Following up with the artifacts (attached) and a short technical appendix below. Attachments: Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2026_summary.pdf; redwood_caIQ_export_2027.csv; medisure_dpia_acknowledgement_signed.pdf (placeholder until Legal signs).

Technical appendix (short):
- No-Train: Redwood's hosted inference stack separates control-plane telemetry from model training pipelines. Customer prompt/response plaintext is not forwarded to any training ingestion job. The technical controls include ingestion ACLs, queue-level segregation, and automated scrubbers on logs that could contain PII. We will provide a one-paragraph legal-technical statement for your DPIA: "Redwood Inference confirms that, for the account specified herein, customer-provided prompts and generated responses will not be used to train or update models made available to other customers. Logs or telemetry retained for operational purposes are excluded from model training pipelines by policy and automated safeguards."
- Retention: Default data retention for prompt/response artifacts is 30 days (configurable). For Dedicated/Private deployments we support shorter retention policies and can configure 0-day retention plus strict ephemeral-mode operation for KV caches.
- HIPAA controls: Encryption at rest with customer-managed KMS available, TLS 1.2+ in transit, audit logging, and optional BAA for qualifying customers.

Let us know if you'd like additional evidence (e.g., redacted logs showing deletion events) or a short screen share to walk through the controls.

-Rishi
